text:
alex: heads up - tried to install redwoodctl on my raspberrypi cluster (arm64 ubuntu) and the binary from releases 0.9.2 fails with "ELF: wrong architecture"
toni: oh https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/releases has linux amd64 by default, we haven't pushed arm64 in that tag yet
alex: ah ok. the installer script `curl -fsSL https://install.redwood.ai | bash` picked amd64 and dropped it into /usr/local/bin so it obviously fails when executed
mira: can you run `file /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` to confirm?
alex: did that: `redwoodctl: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked...`
toni: Oof. Installer should detect `uname -m` and pick the right asset. Thanks for reporting. Is the cluster's PATH picking up the installer location? sometimes we overwrite a homebrew symlink
alex: yes it's in path, tried `rm /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl && curl ...` then chmod +x and same problem. Workaround is to `apt install gh` and `gh release download` from my machine and scp the arm64 binary into place
build-bot: automatic build for linux/arm64 failed on last CI run (job 2345), linking mismatch with musl vs glibc. See CI-2345
mira: we should publish musl and glibc variants, and also make the installer error if arch not supported rather than dropping a wrong binary. (tracking: DEVEX-472)
toni: short-term: release a tarball `redwoodctl-0.9.3-linux-arm64.tar.gz` with glibc build. Also add a flag to the installer: `--force-arch=arm64` so it won't auto-download the wrong one
alex: for anyone hitting this, steps I used:
```
# on my x86 laptop
gh release download v0.9.3 --pattern "*linux-arm64*" --repo redwood-inference/redwoodctl
scp redwoodctl-linux-arm64 pi:/tmp/
sudo mv /tmp/redwoodctl-linux-arm64 /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl
sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl
```
then `redwoodctl version` shows `0.9.3` and works
docs: adding a note to install docs and a FAQ blurb about arm/arch mismatch. Also adding `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` env var tip in the same FAQ: if you use multiple profiles (work vs devbox) set `export REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=devbox` to avoid prompting during login
mira: also observed that `redwoodctl login` will create `~/.redwoodctl/profiles.json` and set a `default` key. If installer drops a config from the release it can clobber existing profiles. We should avoid shipping a default config file in releases (tracking: DEVEX-473)
toni: agreed. I'll cut a hotfix release and bump the installer to validate arch. Assigning to infra team to re-run CI with glibc target
alex: thanks - leaving the manual scp steps in my dotfiles for now. will test the new installer once it's out :thumbsup:
